Part 0 engine: level = 1.0 when Engine+0x2530 & 3 (blown or seized), else the max of the six PU wears +0x254c..+0x2560; part 1 power unit: max of the six wears (no flag override); part 2 gearbox: 1.0 when GearBox+0x658 & 7, else min(0.99, +0x674); later parts: 0x142f17170 for groups 3 and 4, tyres (max wheel +0xf4 of [car+0x580]+0x70..+0x88), aero. Each level goes through its own threshold table in the system ({u32 state, float threshold} pairs: engine +0xc30 count +0xc60, power unit +0xc70 count +0xca0, gearbox +0xcb0 count +0xce0, tyres +0xd70 count +0xda0): the state is the last pair whose threshold <= level. State 5 (terminal) is replaced by 2 unless system+0xf90 is set. Results: record+0x10/+0x14/+0x18 states, +0x3c/+0x40 engine/PU levels. So a blown or seized engine (or a canned ICE failure via wear 1.0) reaches the terminal state only when the system's tables map 1.0 to 5 and +0xf90 allows it. Callers 0x142f16490 (0x142f164c6, #691 VehicleTerminalDamageSystem::updateVehicle) and two .data1 copies. raised by engine-re with --force 2026-11-18 at user request (lane owner review requested)

Only caller 0x143267ab0, which runs it when the TrackSpace system is active and g_Game_TSQuadTree has no tree yet (0x1460bffc0 == 0). So a missing TSQuadTree resource is rebuilt at runtime with these (different) parameters; the shipped vanilla trees follow the offline rule (min(255, floor(L/15.1)) on the main line) instead. 2026-11-17 engine-re, static. raised by engine-re with --force 2026-11-17 at user request (lane owner review requested) | added in parallel as Game_TrackSpace_GenerateRuntimeQuadtree (L1): engine-re 2026-11-17 track round C2 (static d873a1c8): runtime point quadtree over BOTH TrackSpace routes: route splines [[0x146ce5498]+0x28]+0x18 (main) and +0x20 (pit), length = last knot (dist+len) of [spl+0x10]+0x30..+0x38; whole build skipped when either route is null (0x143222bdd/0x143222bea). total points = min(255, (main+pit)/40.0 m) (0x1455cda3c, cap 0x143222c41), split main/pit by length; logs 'Generating quadtree', '+ pit length %.3f km', 'Calculated %d pitlane points...'. Track mods: the TrackSpace pit route is required here, not optional. H: runtime helper, distinct from the stored TSQuadTree resource. | 2026-11-20 engine-re round L2 AI / track-markup size limits (static): the 255 cap (0x143222c41 and the second min at decomp line ~457) matches the u8 point index of the network position anchor (Game_Network_DeserialiseVehicle 0x14326b251/0x14326b25b) and the u8 leaf indices. The rebuild runs only when no tree is loaded, so a shipped TSQuadTree wins; for 20.8 km it gives ~82 m spacing (offline: no effect, no reader). edited by engine-re with --force 2026-11-20 at user request (lane owner review requested)

name: Sess_VirtualPerformance_IngestVpTimes
notes: Slot 38 (+0x130) of vt 0x1458827b0 (VirtualPerformanceSystem), reached only through the VPTimes resource handler (vt 0x145882a20, slot 14 0x1438aac60 jumps to [handler+0x10]->vt+0x130; the shared create body Sess_VpResource_Create_Body calls slot 14 with (key, data, size)). Parses the VPTimes payload (this, key, u32* data, size) until size bytes are used: per table k = 0,1,.. (file order; stock: lap, pit lane) u32 [ignored word, vehicle hash, block count]; table k = std::map at this+0x108[k] (vector grown from heap this+0x100), entry keyed by (key, vehicle hash); an existing entry is cleared first (re-load replaces). Per block an 8-word header [a int, b float, grip float, int (0), c int, mass float, perf float, n] then n float32 samples (stock first sample 0.0); nested maps c -> a -> b -> grip -> word3 -> mass -> perf (0x40/0x48-byte nodes) and the samples are COPIED into a float vector reserved to exactly n (node + vector from this+0x10 = the VIRTUAL_PERFORMANCE heap). No checks on the leading word, the block count, n or monotonic times. So the 4 float axes b/grip/mass/perf are the 2^4 = 16 blended corner blocks of Sess_VirtualPerformance_EvalBlocksAtDistance, and this+0x108 is the table vector Sess_VirtualPerformance_TimeAtDistance indexes with key[0]: the virtual-performance time tables ARE the VPTimes resource (static side of T211). L2 2026-11-17 (engine-re track RE round B2): decomp read and claims checked against the disassembly; refs from an own rel32/riprel (capstone-confirmed)/abs64 scan. raised by engine-re with --force 2026-11-17 at user request (lane owner review requested)

name: Sess_VirtualPerformance_EvalBlocksAtDistance
notes: Tail-jump target of Sess_VirtualPerformance_EvalBlendedTime. d outside 0..route length+0.01 is wrapped with fmodf; route length = float at this+0xa0 + route*0x48. Sample index i = (int)(d / route_length * (n - 1)) and i+1, clamped to n-1, where n = the sample count of the route in the vehicle record (record+0x48 entry +8) - ONE n for all blocks. The same i is used on the float array (+0x30) of every one of the 16 corner blocks of the selection (block+0x20 = axis value), blended linearly over 4 axes. No per-block length check: a block with fewer than n samples is read past its end (track modding: every VPTimes-style block of one table must have the same sample count over the lap). Already listed as a vehicle-slot consumer in Sess_Ai_BuildVehicleRecords. L2 2026-11-17 (engine-re track RE round B): decomp read and claims checked against the disassembly; refs from an own rel32/riprel (capstone-confirmed)/abs64 scan.  | engine-re track RE round B2 2026-11-17 (static): the one n per table comes from Sess_Ai_BuildVehicleRecords (0x1438a3cbb): for table k it walks the vehicle's nested VPTimes maps in key order (smallest c, a, b, grip, word3, mass, perf first) and takes the sample count of the FIRST non-empty block (vector size, 0x1438a3f42 path) into record+0x48 entry k +8. So a short first block shrinks the index range of every block and a short later block is read past its end. | 2026-11-20 engine-re round L2 AI / track-markup size limits (static): no sample cap: n is an int from the record, the sample arrays are heap float vectors, the index is (int)(d/L*(n-1)) in float (exact for n < 2^24). Any density works as long as all blocks of one table have the same n (and n >= 2; n = 1 makes the weight 0/0). The 1 sample per 5 m stock density is not required by code; the only bound is GAME_DEFAULT heap memory (1024 MiB with Swofty heap_sizes).

name: Snd_Run_JobWorkerThread
notes: Audio job worker thread body (12 threads, priority 1). mailbox+0x00 = its thread id. Loop: wait for its wake event (0x14391e3b0); run the mailbox request fn(type, 0) (+0x08 fn, +0x24 type); then while g_Snd_JobWorkerPending != 0, under g_Snd_JobWorkerLock, take the first set flag of overflow slots 0-11 only (unrolled byte compares 0x143fc65ea..0x143fc66e7), clear it, decrement the pending count and run that request outside the lock; finally clear its mailbox busy flag (+0x28). proto: void Ne_PhysMaterial_CombinePair(void *out, const void *matA, const void *matB)
notes: Contact material pair (agent collide, dcso-verify claim 3): sqrt(a*b) for 9 floats +0x04..+0x24 (restitution, friction, cfm, correctionVel, minBounceVel, softness K/S min/max; softness only if one side > 0, a zero side takes the other value); product < 0 -> error 0x14535d734; single-entry cache; called twice from 0x1440f6e20 | gb-verify claim 12: ctx = world+0x20, one cached pair at ctx+0/+8; geometric means +0x14..+0x24 always rewritten; minK/minS/maxK/maxS/speedForMaxSoftness (+0x18..+0x28) only written when mat+0x18 or +0x1c > 0 on a side, else previous pair's values stay (stale cache bug: patched materials need minK/minS > 0); same material -> returns the record itself

name: Ne_Phys_BuildContactRows
notes: Contact rows (agent collide): speed-dependent softness K/S lerp over |v|/speedForMaxSoftness -> erp = dtK/(dtK+S), cfm = 1/(dtK+S); restitution above minBounceVel; impulse cap contact+0x60/dt; angular arm halved on wall-like contacts (|n.y| < 0.2) | gb-verify claim 11: soft contact when contact+0x93 == 0: v = |vA-vB| (body+0x220), t = min(1, v/rec+0x28), K = lerp(+0x18,+0x20), S = lerp(+0x1c,+0x24), both times an island scale s: ERP = dtK/(dtK+S), CFM = 1/(s(dtK+S)); K/S = 1.8e19 sentinel or both 0 -> ERP world+0x118, CFM rec+0xc; bias = max(0, depth+0x58 - world+0x11c)*ERP/dt (capped rec+0x10 when +0x93 != 0)

name: Ne_VcqtcTile_QueryLeaf
proto: bool Ne_VcqtcTile_QueryLeaf(void *tile_obj, void *query, const uint8_t *leaf_ref, const float *box)
notes: VCQTC tile leaf test (2026-11-17 engine-re track runtime round, static). leaf_ref = 2 bytes big-endian: 0xffff = empty; else index = ((b0 & 0x7f) << 8) | b1 into the leaf area [[tile_obj+0x188]+0x40] (4-byte units). Leaf word w (u32): when query+0x29 is set top = (w & 0x7fff) - ((w >> 15) & 0x7ff) - 0x4000 and tall = w >> 26, else top = (w & 0x7fff) - 0x4000 and tall = 0; top_y = top * 2 / 100 (m). If query+0x20 (a y) > top_y the leaf is skipped. Then byte w+4 = total tris, w+5 = ground tris; tri count used = w+5 when query+0x28 is set, else total - tall (tall walls are stored last). The u16 tri indices follow, then one u32 quantised box per tri (x/z relative to the leaf box, +-127) tested against the query box; hits go as a bitmask to the query callback [query]. So H0 (low 15 bits) = 0x4000 + 50*maxY and must not be lower than the leaf's real top, and ground tris must be the first w+5 entries.

name: Ne_VcqtcTile_GatherLeafTriangles
notes: Query callback (pointer at 0x145c05310) that turns the hit bitmask of a VCQTC leaf into world triangles (2026-11-17 engine-re, static). Per hit: u16 tri index from the leaf list, triangle bytes at [[tile_obj+0x188]+0x38] + 4*i: v0 = ((b0 & 3) << 8) | b1, v1 = v0 + b2, v2 = v0 + b3 (16-byte vertices at +0x28); material = pointer slot (b0 >> 2) & 7 of the tile's material array at +0x50. So a tile can address at most 1024 vertices, v1/v2 must lie 0..255 after v0, and a triangle can use only the first 8 materials. Output batch capped at 0x200 triangles (ctx+0x9480.. state); triangles already emitted for this tile are skipped (ctx+0x9054 list).

Each child <Knot> gives position='x,y,z' and up='x,y,z' (comma strtok + atof; up defaults to 0,1,0 when missing or 'undefined'; the position registers are not reset per knot, so a Knot without position repeats the previous position), appended as a 32-byte knot {pos xyz, 0, up xyzw} to a vector that grows 1.5x with no count limit and no checks (no minimum, no spacing, no turn or duplicate test). name: Game_TrackSpace_AddVolumeFromGates
notes: 2026-11-17 engine-re track runtime round 2, static. Called once per XML <Volume> by Game_TrackSpace_LoadXml (0x1445ec55b) with the 2 gates x 4 points: slots 0..3 of gate 0 then gate 1, filled from point4, point3, point2, point1 in that order (parse at 0x1445ec6ed..0x1445ec9e0, store 0x1445ec5bd). When route+0xa0 is set (always 1 when LoadXml creates the 0xa8-byte route) and the distance between the two gates' (slot1 + 0.5*slot2) points is > 100 m, the gates are lerped into n = ceil(d/99.9) pieces (vroundss imm 0xa at 0x1445f2d9d; piece i uses t0 = i*s/d, t1 = min((i+1)*s, d)/d, s = d/n) and the function recurses (correction V10791). Otherwise it appends THREE 0x140-byte volumes to route+0x88..+0x90 (growth 1.5x through allocator route+0x80), built by Game_TrackSpaceVolume_BuildPlanes from the strip between neighbouring points: strip k (k = 0,1,2) uses gate1[k], gate1[k+1], gate0[k+1], gate0[k], i.e. strip 0 = point4..point3, strip 1 = point3..point2, strip 2 = point2..point1. Volume +0x00 u8 = route byte route+0 (0 main, 1 pit), +0x01 u8 = strip index k, +0x04 u32 = own index, +0x134 f32 start distance = previous volume +0x134 + +0x138 (0 for the first), +0x138 f32 length = |+0xd0 - +0xc0| of strip 1; all three strips share start and length. So the car is inside the TrackSpace while it is anywhere between point1 and point4; point2/point3 only split the middle strip (index 1) from the two side strips (0 and 2). raised by engine-re with --force 2026-11-17 at user request (lane owner review requested)
